 (Hon'ble Shri Parth Prateem Sahu, Judge)
 Order on Board
14/08/2024
1.

Applicant has filed this second bail application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S., 2023 for grant of regular bail as he was arrested in connection with Crime No. 870 of 2020 registered at Police Station Sarkanda, Distt. - Bilaspur (C.G.) for offence punishable under Section 420, 467, 468, 471,
34 of I.P.C., 1860.
2.

Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that, complainant Manikdas Manikpuri lodged report in the concerned Police Station alleging that he purchased a land bearing part of khasra No. 1053/87 plot No. 279 from T. D. Sharjal vide registered sale deed dated 18.11.2010.
The said land was subsequently sold by applicant to one Harbati Sharma forging 22 point document issued by Revenue Officials.
Based on the report, aforementioned crime was registered against applicant and he was arrested on 02.03.2024.
3. Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has not committed any offence.
He has been falsely implicated in the aforementioned crime.
Absolutely false and baseless allegations have been levelled against applicant.

The plot which was sold to Harbati Sharma,
Vipin Garg vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157309857/
1 document of which was seized by Police during course of investigation and part of charge-sheet bearing khasra No. 1053/5 and plot No. 289A from which, it is clearly appearing that the land which was sold by applicant to Harbati Sharma is different plot / land and not the plot / land purchased by complainant.

entities.text: Vipin Garg vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also submits that statement of concerned Patwari is recorded by police in which he stated that there is no interpolation in 22 point document issued by him.

Applicant is in jail since 02.03.2024, investigation is complete, charge-sheet is filed, offence is triable by Judicial Magistrate,
trial may take some time for its conclusion, hence, he may be enlarged on bail.

4. Learned State counsel opposes the submission made by learned counsel for applicant and would submits that allegation against applicant is specific that land purchased by complainant was sold by applicant to Harbati Sharma which is the same land.

He also submits that in the statement of President of society recorded by Police, there are other allegations that applicant misrepresenting himself to be vice- president of society has sold many plots.

However, upon asking whether any complaint is made by President of society, he submits that from perusal of case-diary/charge-sheet,
it is appearing that complainant is made by Manikdas Manikpuri and not by President of society 5.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

6. Taking into consideration facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegations, submission of counsel for the respective parties, investigation is complete, charge-sheet if filed, submission of learned State counsel on query that there is no criminal antecedent against applicant, period of pre-trial detention of applicant, offence is triable by Judicial Magistrate, without commenting on merits of the case, I am inclined to enlarge the applicants on bail.
7. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on regular bail, upon furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court on the conditions that - a) Applicant shall appear before the Trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
b) The applicant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c) If the applicant is found involved in similar offence in future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
Certified copy as per rules.

Sd  Sd/-
 (Parth Prateem Sahu)
